cards.name: Stained Glass
cards.summary: Breaks the bitmap into irregular polygonal panes of flat colour (each pane takes the colour of the area under it) separated by solder lines in a chosen colour, with optional 3D lighting that makes the panes and lead lines read as raised glass, like a leaded church window.
use_for: stained-glass / church-window treatment of a photo for festival, wedding or religious posters
decorative mosaic backgrounds made from any photo or gradient
abstracting a busy photo so it sits behind headline type without competing
PowerClip the result into an arched window shape for a convincing glass panel
avoid: small type, thin lines or faces that must stay recognisable: panes average them away (on the vector plate the 'PGD' type and the thin zigzag stroke break up); use a smaller Size, or Effects/Creative/Crystalize for the same polygon cells without outlines

you want cells without lead lines: use Effects/Creative/Crystalize (Solder Width 0, the range minimum, presumably drops the lines but was not render-checked; Mosaic is no alternative, it sets tiles on a grout colour)

scripted runs: this effect's command string was not applied in a harvest test, and the same format did nothing for Pixelate and Invert, so check that pixels actually changed; Solder Color has no key in the harvested command template, so set it in the dialog
the scripted path only takes a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vectors to bitmap first or use the menu route

params.name: Size
params.does: size of each glass pane: higher = fewer, larger panes and more abstraction

params.name: Thickness
params.does: Solder Width: thickness of the lead lines between panes (0 is the range minimum; that it removes the lines is not render-checked)

params.name: LightIntensity
params.does: Light Intensity: how much light shines through the glass; higher values brighten the panes (approximate, not render-checked)

params.name: BorderColorItem
params.does: Solder Color: colour of the lead lines; black or dark grey reads as real lead, gold or white for a decorative look

params.name: 3DLighting
params.does: 3D Lighting: adds bevel-like lighting so panes and solder look raised
params.typical: on for a realistic window, off for a flat graphic (default off)

pairs_with: Effects/Adjust/Brightness/Contrast/Intensity (brighten the source first so panes glow)
Effects/Blur/Gaussian Blur (a light blur first gives cleaner, flatter pane colours)
Object/PowerClip/Place Inside Frame (clip into an arch or circle window)
cards.scripting: On a bitmap shape s (Shape.Bitmap): s.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("PGD Stained Glass", "StainedGlassEffect Size=40,Thickness=8,LightIntensity=4,3DLighting=1") (format from the harvested cmd_template; this effect's string was not applied in a test, and the bool spelling 0/1 is not proven; Solder Color has no command key). ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not apply (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed no pixels), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("3c485239-ab86-45d4-8d10-9a02c3e35e5a") opens the effect's dialog on the selection (modal: a person sets the values and presses OK), so it is not an unattended route.
cards.non_destructive: menu route: yes, CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack (Properties docker, ApplyOrDeleteEffect:StainedGlassEffect; editable or removable); the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changed the bitmap's pixels in the harvest tests and undo restored them; whether it also leaves a stack entry was not checked
cards.cost: moderate on a 1920x1080 bitmap; 3D Lighting adds a little (untimed estimate)

review.changes: avoid: the plate note named the Photoshop photo plate's strip; now the CorelDRAW vector plate's 'PGD' type and zigzag; 'use Mosaic for cells without lead lines' was wrong (Mosaic sets tiles on grout), now Crystalize with its path; Solder Width 0 'removes the lines' and Light Intensity behaviour marked as not render-checked; scripting: dropped the unharvested 'Shape.Type 5', InvokeItem opens the modal dialog (it does not apply silently with current values), added that ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK on an unapplied string; non_destructive no longer asserts the scripted path is undo-only (stack entry not checked); cost marked as an untimed estimate

verified.note: The plate became leaded glass: large irregular panes of flat colour separated by thick black solder lines, with a light bevel highlight on the pane edges from 3D lighting, like a church window.

cards.name: Vignette
cards.summary: Frames the bitmap with an ellipse, circle, rectangle or square: everything outside the shape is filled with black, white or a chosen colour that fades softly into the picture, the classic portrait or old-photo vignette.
use_for: soft white oval frame for a portrait, wedding or memorial card
black vignette that pulls attention to the centre of a hero photo
colour-matched frame (Other colour) so a photo melts into a poster background of the same colour
vintage / old-photo look together with a sepia or tint adjustment
avoid: anything important near the edges (captions, logos; on the vector plate the zigzag and the 'PGD' type along the bottom): it is covered by the frame colour

a subtle darkening of the corners only: the frame colour is painted over the image rather than darkening it (not render-checked), so use Toolbox/Transparency/Fountain Transparency on a black shape over the photo, or Photoshop's Lens Correction Vignette Amount
an off-centre focus: no position parameter was harvested, so the shape sits centred; PowerClip or a transparency gives control
scripted runs: defaults and Offset / Fade ranges were not read (the data source exists only while the dialog is open) and this effect's command string was not applied in a test; check the pixels

params.name: ColorMode
params.does: frame colour: Black, White, or Other (uses ColorItem)
params.typical: Black for drama, White for soft portrait cards

params.name: ColorItem
params.does: the frame colour when ColorMode is Other

params.name: Shape
params.does: shape of the clear area: Ellipse (presumably follows the image proportions), Circle, Rectangle or Square

params.name: Offset
params.does: how far the frame reaches in from the edges, i.e. the size of the clear centre (exact direction and range not harvested)
params.typical: mid-range; compare in the dialog preview

params.name: Fade
params.does: width of the soft transition between the frame colour and the image; low = hard-edged cut-out, high = gentle fade
params.typical: mid to high for a soft vignette (range not harvested)

pairs_with: Effects/Adjust/Brightness/Contrast/Intensity (lift the centre after a black vignette)
Toolbox/Transparency/Fountain Transparency (a softer, see-through alternative or extra layer)
Object/PowerClip/Place Inside Frame (vignette a photo inside a custom frame shape)

cards.name: Vortex
cards.summary: Repaints the bitmap with short brush streaks whose direction swirls around the centre: on the 2026-10 gallery render (Size 30, Inner Direction 90, Outer Direction 270) the whole plate became a combed, brushed texture whose strokes curve around a point in the middle of the frame and run diagonally or across toward the edges, while the picture itself is not twisted (the mid-tones, stripes and the colour strip stay in place, softened and streaky). Inner and Outer Direction set the stroke direction at the centre and at the edges, Size the stroke size, and Style picks the stroke character (its list was not harvested).
use_for: painterly brushed treatment of a photo whose strokes circle a centre, for posters or album art
energy or motion texture behind a headline where the photo only supplies colour
abstract brushed textures for packaging or music artwork
avoid: faces, text or logos that must stay crisp: the brush streaks soften and streak them

a twisted, whirlpool-shaped image: Vortex does not move the picture, only its brush strokes swirl; use Effects/Distort/Swirl (Whirlpool for fluid streaks); Photoshop's Twirl is that geometric twist, not this brush-streak effect

scripted runs: the Style list values were not harvested, so leave Style out (the dialog's current style is used); no centre-point parameter was harvested; this effect's command string was not applied in a test

params.name: Style
params.does: stroke style of the swirl (list not read by the harvest)

params.name: Size
params.does: size of the swirl strokes / detail: higher values give bolder, more destructive streaks (approximate)

params.name: InnerDirection
params.does: rotation direction of the inner part of the vortex, as a compass angle
params.typical: 0-360 deg in 5 deg steps (default 180); setting it opposite to Outer Direction for a stronger twist is untested

params.name: OuterDirection
params.does: rotation direction of the outer part of the vortex, as a compass angle

pairs_with: Effects/Blur/Gaussian Blur (soften the streaks into a smooth abstract)
Effects/Adjust/Brightness/Contrast/Intensity (punch up the colours of the swirl)
Object/PowerClip/Place Inside Frame (use the swirl as a fill inside type or shapes)

ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not apply (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed no pixels), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("c7f8d93b-619a-4a34-b49b-93cd9023d334") opens the effect's dialog on the selection (modal: a person sets the values and presses OK), so it is not an unattended route.

cards.cost: moderate to heavy on a 1920x1080 bitmap at large Size (untimed estimate)

review.changes: equivalents: removed PS twirl (the card itself says the geometric twist is Effects/Distort/Swirl, whose card already maps PS twirl; Vortex smears into brush streaks, a different result), noted in avoid instead; 'opposite directions give the strongest twist' marked untested; 5 deg step added from the batch; scripting: dropped 'Shape.Type 5', InvokeItem opens the modal dialog, added the unapplied-string warning; non_destructive qualified; cost marked as an untimed estimate

second_opinion.note: Re-opened at 3x in six regions: the brush strokes curve around the frame centre and run diagonally / across toward the edges while mid-tones and stripes stay in place; harness check: all three keys were read (each probe moved the pixels) and Style was left at the dialog's stored value, so the brushwork-only result is the effect, not a dropped twist key.

cards.name: Band Pass
cards.summary: Frequency filter meant to rebalance fine detail (edges, texture, noise) against smooth areas by passing a band of detail sizes. On the 2026-10 gallery render (Frequency = InWeight 25, Bandwidth = MidWeight 50) the visible result was an even darkening of the whole photo to about 79 % of its brightness (white 247 -> 198, mid grey 128 -> 101, the red swatch 232,32,42 -> 183,25,33) with detail and edges much as before; both keys are read (InWeight 100 or MidWeight 100 move the result by about 70 levels) but those looks were not inspected, so how the sliders map onto the band is still not verified.
use_for: pulling out texture and edges from a soft photo for a gritty or technical look
reducing fine noise while keeping mid-size shapes
experimental frequency-split looks before tinting or posterizing
avoid: expecting edge or texture emphasis from low values: InWeight 25 / MidWeight 50 only darkened the photo evenly on the render
ordinary sharpening: use Effects/Sharpen/Unsharp Mask or Adaptive Unsharp, which are predictable
an edges-only grey look: Effects/Sharpen/High Pass is simpler
scripted runs: no min / max was harvested for either slider and this effect's command string was not applied in a test; preview in the dialog and check the pixels
flat-colour vector art such as the vector plate (convert to bitmap first): broad flat areas hold almost no detail, so results there may look flat or grey (not render-checked)

params.name: InWeight
params.does: Frequency: where the passed band sits in detail size; the key name suggests the weight of the inner (smooth, low-frequency) band, so lowering it is expected to flatten broad tones (not verified)
params.typical: default 100 (range not harvested; whether 100 is neutral is not known)

params.name: MidWeight
params.does: Bandwidth: how wide the band of kept detail sizes is; the key name suggests the weight of the middle band (not verified)
params.typical: default 100 (range not harvested; whether 100 is neutral is not known)

pairs_with: Effects/Transform/Posterize (graphic look from the filtered detail)
cards.scripting: On a bitmap shape s (Shape.Bitmap): s.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("PGD Band Pass", "BandPassEffect InWeight=25,MidWeight=50") (format from the harvested cmd_template; not applied in a test for this effect; 25 / 50 are guesses because no range was harvested). ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not apply (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed no pixels), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("ff110df4-be9e-405e-93ac-2a1b2ca7df5b") opens the effect's dialog on the selection (modal: a person sets the values and presses OK), so it is not an unattended route.
cards.non_destructive: menu route: yes, CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack (Properties docker, ApplyOrDeleteEffect:BandPassEffect; editable or removable); the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changed the bitmap's pixels in the harvest tests and undo restored them; whether it also leaves a stack entry was not checked
cards.cost: moderate (frequency filtering over the whole bitmap; untimed estimate)

review.changes: avoid: the 'soft plate photo' line described the Photoshop plate; now the CorelDRAW vector plate (flat colour); typical no longer implies 100 is a no-op ('lower it to see an effect' was unverified); scripting: dropped 'Shape.Type 5', demo values flagged as unranged guesses, InvokeItem opens the modal dialog, added the unapplied-string warning; non_destructive qualified; cost marked as an untimed estimate

verified.note: No visible edge or texture emphasis: at Frequency (InWeight) 25 and Bandwidth (MidWeight) 50 the photo is evenly darkened to about 79 % of its brightness (white 247 -> 198, mid grey 128 -> 101, red swatch 232,32,42 -> 183,25,33) with detail much as before; summary and look rewritten to what the frame shows.

second_opinion.note: Re-sampled: every sampled colour is about 0.79 x its ref value with detail unchanged, consistent with the low-frequency weight (InWeight 25 %) scaling the base tones; harness check: both keys were read (each at 100 moves the pixels by about 70), so the even darkening is the effect at these values, not an ignored command.

cards.name: Bump Map
cards.summary: Gives the bitmap a raised, embossed surface by treating a bump-map pattern's brightness as height and lighting it with a directional and an ambient light, so the picture looks printed on or pressed into a textured material (stretched once or tiled). On the 2026-10 gallery render (Tile, ScaleFactor 150, directional light 90, ambient 50, with the dialog's stored map) the photo sits under a fine regular square relief grid, about 20 % darker overall; without the two brightness keys the same render came out near black (mean 27 of 255). The 2026-10-04 audit, run with whatever map the dialog held, saw ScaleFactor 30.85 vs 170.15 give different, repeatable pixels (mean difference 6.82).
use_for: photo printed on a textured surface (stucco, canvas, embossed paper) for posters and packaging
tiled relief patterns over a flat image for backgrounds
relit, embossed texture plates with coloured light for title cards
avoid: faces and fine type: the pattern's relief and lighting run straight across them, and the audit saw a heavy overall change even at a low Scale Factor; mask the effect or apply it to the background only
relief built from the image itself rather than a pattern: use Effects/3D Effects/Emboss

a predictable subtle result: on the test photo the audit changed the pixels by 73 (mean, of 255) at ScaleFactor 30.85 and 77.35 at 200, so Scale Factor is not the lever for subtlety; preview and change the map or the light brightness instead (raising DirectionalLightBrightness to 90 and AmbientLightBrightness to 50 lifted the gallery render from near black, mean 27, to a readable 83)

scripted runs: only ScaleFactor was proven in a command string; the bump-map image, preset and the light colours have no harvested values, so the dialog's stored map is used; ScaleFactor=810 was accepted by script (not clamped, not rejected: 1.81 from the 200 result), but stay inside the dialog's 1-200

params.name: TileHeight

params.name: Invert

params.name: Smooth

params.name: Ceiling

params.name: Highlight

params.name: Direction

params.typical: 0-360; which angle points where was not harvested

params.name: Declination

cards.name: User Defined
cards.summary: Custom 5x5 convolution filter: you type weights into a 5x5 kernel grid (Kernel_00 to Kernel_44, centre Kernel_22) and each pixel becomes the weighted sum of its neighbours divided by Divisor plus Offset, so one dialog can sharpen, blur, emboss or detect edges. The default kernel (centre 5, the four direct neighbours -1, preset 'High Pass 2') sharpens.
use_for: precise, repeatable sharpening or blurring with known numbers (house-style image processing)
emboss / relief and directional edge effects by hand-built asymmetric kernels
edge-detection plates for line-art or engraving looks
reproducing a convolution recipe from another tool exactly
avoid: kernels whose weights sum to 0 with Offset 0: the image goes almost black; add Offset (about 128 for mid-grey) or keep the sum at 1
directional kernels with Symmetric kernel on: it presumably mirrors your entries and cancels the direction; switch it off first
everyday sharpening or blur: Effects/Sharpen/Unsharp Mask and Effects/Blur/Gaussian Blur are faster to tune

scripted runs: 31 keys and this effect's command string was not applied in a test; send every kernel cell you need, because unsent cells keep the dialog's current values (the default kernel has non-zero cells)

params.name: Kernel_22
params.does: centre weight of the 5x5 kernel; Kernel_rc is read as row r, column c (0-4), an assumption: the default kernel is symmetric, so the harvest cannot tell row from column
params.typical: 5 sharpen (default), 1 with neighbours 1 for blur, 0 for edge or emboss kernels

params.name: Kernel_12
params.does: an edge neighbour of the centre (above it if the first digit is the row; likewise Kernel_21, Kernel_23, Kernel_32 are the other three)

params.name: Kernel_00
params.does: corner weight two pixels up-left; outer-ring cells widen the filter to 5x5
params.typical: 0, or negative with a positive Kernel_44 for a diagonal emboss

params.name: Divisor
params.does: the weighted sum is divided by this; set it to the kernel sum to keep brightness

params.name: Offset
params.does: added to every result after dividing; lifts zero-sum kernels to mid-grey
params.typical: 0, or 128 for emboss and edge kernels

params.name: AutoDivisor
params.does: Auto compute divisor: sets Divisor to the kernel sum automatically
params.typical: on (default) for blur and sharpen, off for zero-sum kernels

params.name: PreserveColors
params.does: Preserve colors: keeps the original colours and applies the filter to brightness only (approximate)

params.name: SymmetricKernel
params.does: Symmetric kernel: presumably mirrors an entry into its symmetric cells (behaviour inferred from the caption)
params.typical: on (default) for blur and sharpen, off for directional kernels

params.name: Preset
params.does: loads a saved kernel: High Pass 2 (default), Blur (3x3 Mask), Blur (5x5 Mask)

pairs_with: Effects/Sharpen/High Pass (ready-made alternative for edge looks)
Effects/Adjust/Brightness/Contrast/Intensity (tune the grey level of an emboss result)

ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not apply (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed no pixels), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("e634b694-e2ec-4291-bac9-d1cc7900e6c5") opens the effect's dialog on the selection (modal: a person sets the values and presses OK), so it is not an unattended route.
cards.non_destructive: menu route: yes, CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack (Properties docker, ApplyOrDeleteEffect:UserDefinedEffect; editable or removable); the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changed the bitmap's pixels in the harvest tests and undo restored them; whether it also leaves a stack entry was not checked

review.changes: Kernel_rc row/column reading and 'Kernel_12 = above the centre' marked as an assumption (the symmetric default kernel cannot show the order; the diagonal demo is unaffected); Symmetric kernel mirroring hedged as inferred from the caption; scripting: dropped 'Shape.Type 5', InvokeItem opens the modal dialog, added the unapplied-string warning; non_destructive qualified; cost marked as an untimed estimate; kernel defaults, ranges, demo and PS custom checked and kept

verified.note: The custom kernel turned the plate into a mid-grey (Offset 128) embossed relief: edges become raised light and dark ridges with colour fringes on the stripes and swatch borders, one of the looks the card lists; SymmetricKernel, AutoDivisor and Divisor were ignored by the script (dropped).
